title: Seller-Ops Emergency Handbook - pilot sprint triage (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, field-friendly emergency handbook for Seller-Ops and SEs running pilot sprints. Not a replacement for SRE runbooks — this is the seller-facing triage script, canned messaging, and rapid decision heuristics to keep pilots healthy and customers calm while we escalate.

Audience:
- Seller (field SE/AE) doing live demo or pilot
- Seller-Ops on call during pilot ramp
- SE escalation to platform/RTE/SRE

Goals (what this doc should do):
- Give sellers a two-minute triage checklist to stabilize a pilot
- Provide neutral, factual language for status updates to customers
- Offer quick fallbacks (model variants, capacity options) with concrete cost/latency tradeoffs
- Define clear handoff notes to engineering and SREs so they can act immediately

Top-line heuristics (two-sentence summary to memorize):
- If latency > SLA or errors > 1%: switch routing to fallback model variant and enable short-lived burst capacity; notify platform via #pilot-oncall with CORP subject line.
- If output quality regresses: capture 10 representative prompts + responses, flag "quality-regression" in Jira, and pause aggressive caching while we collect evals.

Quick triage checklist (do in order, ~2–8 mins):
1) Confirm scope: which route/model/region is impacted? Ask customer: "Which API path are you calling?"
2) Check status dashboard: model instance health, queue depth, per-route latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) — screenshot p95.
3) Switch routing policy: route requests to fallback compatible variant (e.g., redwood-gpt-small-v2) and roll traffic 10-30% then 100% if stable.
4) Toggle caching/batching: temporarily disable prefix caching if outputs look stale; if tokens are spiking, lower batch target size.
5) If capacity-limited: enable burst capacity (Dedicated customers: offer a 4–hour reserved burst with agreed rate; Hosted: use region failover).
6) Communicate: copy the canned status template below to customer + internal channels.

Canned status updates (short, editable):
- Customer-facing (slack/email):
  Subject: Quick update on your pilot (latency issues)
  Body: Hi <Name>, we’ve detected increased latency on your pilot traffic in region <X>. We’ve routed a portion of traffic to a compatible model variant and enabled short-term burst capacity to keep the experience responsive. No data was exposed or changed. We’ll follow up with a timeline and next steps in 30–60 minutes. — <Seller name>
- Internal (slack #pilot-oncall):
  Title: [PILOT TRIAGE] <Acct> - high latency p95 > X ms
  Steps taken: routed -> redwood-small-v2 (30%), burst enabled in us-west-2, disabled prefix cache for route /chat, collected traces and 12 sample requests.
  Action needed: SRE look into queue growth and kernel saturation, Platform look into autoscaler behavior.

Handoff bundle to attach to Jira (when escalating):
- 10 example requests (timestamp, route, prompt, response)
- Screenshot: model health dashboard, p95/p99 graph
- API request IDs (if available)
- Timing: when fallback was enabled and traffic %
- Customer impact statement (concise)

Fallback options cheat sheet (choose one, then escalate):
- Fallback A: Compatible smaller model (redwood-base-quant): pros = lower latency, lower cost; cons = lower accuracy on long-context prompt types. Use if latency or GPU OOM.
- Fallback B: Regional failover (eu -> us): pros = immediate capacity; cons = may increase network latency and cost.
- Fallback C: Burst capacity (Dedicated): pros = maintains model, preserves accuracy; cons = billable surge, requires sales authorization for extended use.

Buyer objection scripts (short answers):
- "Your model quality dropped": "We temporarily routed traffic to a compatibility variant to ensure responsiveness. We’ve collected examples and our engineering team is investigating root cause — we’ll share findings and rollback plan within the hour."
- "I can’t accept extra charges": "We can limit burst to 1–2 hours while we stabilize, or route a percentage of non-critical traffic to the lower-cost variant until the underlying issue is fixed."

Sample slide skeleton (for a 3-slide crisis update deck):
- Slide 1: One-line impact: customer + metric (p95/err rate) + what we did (fallback/burst).
- Slide 2: What we saw (screenshots + sample prompts) + customer impact.
- Slide 3: Next steps + timeline + point-of-contact.
Speaker notes: keep it factual, avoid speculation on root cause, promise specific times for follow-ups (30/60/120 min).

Quick playbook for quality regression (non-latency):
1) Snapshot: save current model commit and config.
2) Collect golden prompts + customer prompts (20–50) and attach.
3) Run quick A/B (fallback variant vs current) with automated evals (syntactic/semantic metrics we use): if fallback beats current on key metrics, roll to fallback and open a regression investigation.

Customer-facing test checklist (to limit noisy repros):
- Confirm reproducible prompt and time window.
- Ask for exact request IDs (helps correlate logs).
- Reproduce in isolated sandbox with same model version and routing rules.

Templates and snippets (copy/paste):
- Slack to #pilot-oncall: [PILOT TRIAGE] <Acct> | issue: latency | route: /v1/chat | actions: fallback->redwood-small-v2(30%), burst(us-west-2) | samples attached | needs SRE
- Email to customer: Hi <Name>, quick update: we’ve applied a short-term routing change to reduce latency. No content changes; we’ll confirm resolution shortly.

Open questions / TODO (notes to self):
- Who approves burst > 4 hours for a demo pilot? (billing op vs seller) -> ACTION: ask finance ops.
- Add standard parsing script to redact PII from collected prompts before sharing with eng.
- Create a lightweight dashboard view that shows "pilot mode" routes prioritized and a single-click rollback.

Examples of real short-form case logs (anonymized):
- Case 1: Acct ACME-123 — p95 jumped from 400ms -> 2.3s after onboarding cache update; remedied by fallback and cache disable.
- Case 2: Acct PAYSAFE — quality drift after model upgrade; rolled back to previous commit and created regression ticket INF-7821.

Suggested next steps for this doc (small, actionable):
- Iterate with SRE to confirm runbook steps and exact dashboard elements we reference (due: 2025-02-20).
- Add one-pagers for each common fallback model with expected cost delta per 1M tokens.
- Build quick-copy templates in Notion/Confluence and wire a Slack slash command to insert the canned messages.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep language calm and avoid words like "outage" unless we hit firm outage criteria.
- This should fit on a single printed sheet for field sellers.
- Save as slide deck later if demand from AE/SE team is high.

Linked references (for the engineering handoff):
- Quick runbook: CONF-SEC-2154
- Existing pilot escalation playbook: JIRA-INF-7842
- PR with previous canned messages: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/pull/21

Version history (short):
- 2025-01-18: initial draft by Aisha Patel
- 2025-01-24: added fallback cheat sheet after chat with Marco
- 2025-02-10: revised canned messages and added handoff bundle checklist

End of draft.

-- Aisha
summary: Compact field triage handbook for sellers running pilot sprints: checklist, canned messaging, fallback options, handoff bundle, and TODOs.
